title: Research: prove a sharp reader floor for projectively TU queries
body:
## Summary

Prove a sharp actual-reader floor for any finite number of Gram-I plane-indicator targets when the complete query coefficient matrix is a nonzero diagonal row/column scaling of an integer totally unimodular matrix. Readers can be arbitrary on all ports. The theorem holds over every coefficient field and any finite even binary-orthonormal partition. The literal P112 whole-K floor remains 224.

```text
Q = D A E, A totally unimodular
active target-axis span over F -> same axis span over F2
query supports unchanged; reader supports shrink
expanded identity rank -> full original reader tariff
```

This adds arbitrary-target structural coverage beyond PR3463's pair-span theorem and PR3475's seven-ray triple census. DreamingOfClouds/PR2111 assumes a TU signing of the pairing matrix instead; an explicit Gram-I4 geometry with an F7 contraction separates those hypotheses. Public comparisons carry exact heads, blobs, SHA256 and attribution in COMPARISONS.json, without adding them as executable or publication-ancestry dependencies.

Only the new `research/p112-regular-query-floor/` package changes. Credit Tekalign/PR3370 for the unchanged retained partition, Philippe Van Velzen for the prior integral floor, Arham Tahir/PR3345 for the source-bound expanded-identity corroboration, and the P112/query/reader/native lineage in README.md.

## Evidence

- Before: arbitrary larger query dictionaries with global readers were outside the preceding pair/triple results. After: the written support-transfer theorem covers all projectively TU dictionaries, including graph and network queries, at arbitrary finite sizes.
- Two separate implementations agree on all 3,000 minors, 12,288 ordered subset/axis span requests and every literal P112 reader bill. Primary span checks run over Q, F2, F3 and F5. Three original/transferred operators each pass all 12,544 entries; expanded I224 passes all 50,176 entries.
- Four behavioral groups pass, including an omitted actual reader, nonregular triangle transfer failure, capacity/field rejection, six real optimized CLI corruptions and a restored replay. The eight-label F7 contraction is checked separately from the written nonrepresentability proof.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay passed before a string-literal wrap in `verify.py` and one added nonintegral-field rejection case in `test_controls.py`. The wrap preserves the AST; the added case passed the final precommit controls. Exact committed-byte/source-history and official export checks pass at `42730bdda814800a410bdd246a019bab6df36dc6`. All three complete scientific commands pass from that final-head Git-free export, and all 13 exported files remain byte-identical afterward. Strict Ruff diagnostics/formatting pass. Earlier registered bytes are not claimed identical to the final head.

```sh
python3.12 -I -Werror -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-regular-query-floor
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/p112-regular-query-floor/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/p112-regular-query-floor/independent.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/p112-regular-query-floor/test_controls.py
```

Canonical main is `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`, priority revision 6, unchanged at submission refresh. Source binding/arithmetic and card ceiling controls pass separately. No full selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or hosted-CI result is claimed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** isolated.

This is a scoped support-tariff obstruction, not a native supplier or kappa improvement. Nonregular dictionaries, external query dimensions and nonadditive native sharing are outside its hypotheses. Physical acquisition, coefficients, frames, restoration, ownership, hosting, stock, precision, all-size/compiler and outer-transfer obligations remain separate. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The selected frontier is unchanged.
